clue.text: A tot made ready for bed

definitions.text: A tot made ready for bed

parts.words: A tot made ready for bed
parts.note: not a small child being bathed and tucked up but a tot of spirits, a small drink taken just before going to sleep

explanation.surface: A toddler is bathed, put in pyjamas and got ready for bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' wants to be a small child; it is a small measure of whisky or rum.
explanation.definitionFit: A small alcoholic drink taken at bedtime is the traditional sense of the word.

clue.text: They show the purpose of living like nomads

definitions.meaning: aims and purposes, the things that show what someone means to do
nomads live under canvas, so a split phrase of two words describes their dwelling

explanation.surface: Wandering tribes reveal their aims by the way they live.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as two words, IN TENTS, which is how nomads live.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for aims or purposes; split in two it places someone under canvas, as nomads are.

clue.text: Colourful character of pantomime

parts.note: the chequered, multicoloured clown-lover figure of the traditional ..., part of British Christmas pantomime

explanation.surface: A vivid stage figure from a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourful' works both literally (his costume of coloured diamonds) and as 'flamboyant'. Pantomime is the British family Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamond-patterned servant figure of commedia dell'arte and the old British harlequinade is the best-known costumed lead.

clue.text: Having talent many go to the bar

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a lever is a rigid bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: Gifted people often end up going to the bar, as barristers or drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to' simply joins C to LEVER; 'the bar' suggests the legal profession or a pub, but it is a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted or able is bright and quick, a synonym.

clue.text: In theory are they not so funny ?

definitions.text: In theory are they not so funny ?

parts.words: In theory are they not so funny ?
parts.note: pranksters playing tricks on people are meant to be amusing, but the victims rarely find the jokes so funny; in theory versus in practice

explanation.surface: A musing on whether certain comics are less amusing than they claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In theory' sets up its opposite, practical: these jokers deal in practice, not theory, and their pranks are funnier to them than to anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Pranksters who play tricks such as whoopee cushions are known by this idiom.

clue.text: Order of play, quick!

definitions.meaning: a tempo marking on a score is an instruction to the players, telling them to play very fast
the conjuror's exclamation, as in hey ..., said when something happens instantly

explanation.surface: Someone barks at the cast to get the running order moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian musical direction meaning very fast, and the magician's word of sudden transformation.

clue.text: Belloc's hippo-hide won't flatten bullets made of this metal

definitions.text: Belloc's hippo-hide won't flatten bullets made of this metal

parts.words: Belloc's hippo-hide won't flatten bullets made of this metal
parts.note: refers to Hilaire Belloc's comic verse in which the hunter shoots the hippopotamus with bullets of a precious metal, because leaden ones would be flattened by its hide

explanation.surface: A hunter's note that a hippo's thick skin cannot dent bullets of a certain metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Belloc's 'The Hippopotamus' (Bad Child's Book of Beasts): 'I shoot the Hippopotamus / with bullets made of platinum, / because if I use leaden ones / his hide is sure to flatten 'em.'
explanation.definitionFit: The precious white metal is the one named in the rhyme, chosen for its hardness and expense.

clue.text: Ayesha was here for a drink?

parts.note: Ayesha is the immortal queen of H. Rider Haggard's novel She, known as She-who-must-be-obeyed
has been is the perfect form of was, giving the participle

explanation.surface: A woman named Ayesha dropped in somewhere for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a place: 'here' is where one goes for a drink. A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or South African bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit drinking den, so a place you visit to get a drink.

clue.text: Dr Grace's excessive prescriptions ?

parts.note: W. G. Grace, the bearded Victorian cricketer, was also a medical doctor; the overs he bowled could be called his doses, so too-large doses suit him

explanation.surface: A doctor named Grace is accused of overprescribing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr W. G. Grace was England's great Victorian cricketer and a GP; an over is a set of six balls in cricket, so split the answer as OVER DOSES for his medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive amounts of a drug, which is what overprescribing gives a patient.

clue.text: Laurence's follower troubled Ernest

indicators.note: troubled means upset or disturbed, so the name Ernest is jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Ernest who walks behind Laurence is worried.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy; his surname follows his first name, hence 'follower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's surname comes straight after the forename Laurence, as a follower does.

clue.text: A new bed made by a novel carpenter

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of bed and made are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A carpenter makes a new bed, the way an inventive craftsman would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'original'; it means a character in a novel. Adam Bede is the carpenter hero of George Eliot's book.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's title character works as a carpenter, so he is a carpenter from fiction.

clue.text: Concern for a principal product

definitions.meaning: a stake or involvement, as in having a share in a business
the money produced by a principal sum, the capital lent or invested

explanation.surface: A firm worries about its main product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like 'main'; it is the capital sum on which a return is earned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake in a business, and the return money earns on capital, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Truly how a promise's worth is proved

definitions.meaning: an adverb of emphasis: really, certainly

definitions.text: how a promise's worth is proved
definitions.meaning: a promise is only proved by action, by doing it, in two words: in action

explanation.surface: Proof of a promise is in actually keeping it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN DEED: words are proved in deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic adverb meaning really; as two words it means through action, as promises are tested.

clue.text: Publication for children

definitions.meaning: an edition of a magazine or newspaper
offspring, a legal term for descendants

explanation.surface: A magazine number aimed at young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link; 'Publication for children' looks like a children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A single edition of a periodical, and offspring as in 'died without' them.

clue.text: Where ignorance is no light matter

definitions.text: Where ignorance is no light matter

parts.words: Where ignorance is no light matter
parts.note: the idiom for not knowing is literally being somewhere without any light

explanation.surface: Not knowing things can be a serious business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no light matter' means serious, but literally it is where there is no light.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being uninformed is also literal unlit darkness.

clue.text: Fresh coup includes 100 workers who are in possession

indicators.note: includes means the shuffled letters take something within them
fresh suggests a new version, so the word coup is rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A new coup brings in a hundred workers who take possession.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the word after 'Fresh' is OCUP, and 'includes' sets the hundred inside it; 'workers' is the crossword's usual insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupiers or residents are those holding a place, i.e. holding it as theirs.

clue.text: Royal Navy has trouble with Israeli transports

indicators.note: having trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and mixed together

explanation.surface: The British navy is having difficulties with Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: RN and ISRAELI are shuffled together as one pool of nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Passenger planes are carriers, means of transport, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Hospital attire kept in this ?

parts.note: a ward is a room or section of a hospital
a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: A question about where hospital gowns are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: WARD plus ROBE, and clothes are kept in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard for hanging clothes, so attire is stored inside.

clue.text: Railway device holds the record

definitions.meaning: a rotating platform for turning locomotives round
the revolving deck of a record player, on which a vinyl disc sits

explanation.surface: A railway gadget is the holder of a world record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds the record' sounds like a champion; it is the spinning plate of a gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating railway platform for engines, and the spinning deck of a record player.

clue.text: In balance in Germany I must be best off

indicators.note: In tells us one piece sits inside the other, the German word placed within

parts.note: the balance is what remains, the rest
ich is the German word for I

explanation.surface: Someone in Germany decides they must be the most comfortable of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start puts ICH, German for I, into REST, the balance or remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthiest means best off in money terms, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Journalists, 12, would be dispirited

indicators.note: would be says what this word becomes once placed in a deed, so removing that deed recovers it

parts.note: dispirited means low or depressed
12 across is IN DEED, read as an instruction to put this word inside DEED

explanation.surface: Journalists, honestly, would be depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the trick: 12 across, read as two words, is an instruction to place this answer inside a deed, and the word that results means dispirited.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective name for newspapers and those who write for them.

clue.text: Colourful displays of various carpets

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of carpets are mixed

explanation.surface: An assortment of rugs makes a bright show.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of colour from a prism or rainbow are a classic colourful sight.

clue.text: A soldier in trouble is far from 6 ac

indicators.note: in places the A and the soldier inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in difficulty is a long way from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is PRESTO, very fast; a slow tempo marking is far from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow musical tempo is the opposite end from very fast.

clue.text: Mathematician due to return round about £1

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the other letters
to return means go back, so the word due is read backwards

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
L is the pound sign's letter (libra) and 1 is I

explanation.surface: A mathematician owes a refund of around a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' gives EUD; 'round' wraps it around C, L and I. L for pound comes from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek geometer of Alexandria is the classic ancient mathematician.

clue.text: Grandfather clock?

parts.note: a grandfather is a veteran, an elderly person, and a clock is a timer, so an aged timer

explanation.surface: A tall pendulum clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The longcase clock reads as an elderly timepiece; a veteran or elderly person is called by the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly or long-serving person is a veteran, as a grandfather often is.

clue.text: Neat: code cracked by a raconteur

indicators.note: cracked suggests something broken apart, so neat and code are jumbled

explanation.surface: A storyteller breaks a neat code.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is elliptical: what is told by a raconteur, a short story.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a teller of amusing short tales, so the thing told by one.

clue.text: Those of Omar were " Star-scattered on the Grass "

definitions.text: Those of Omar were " Star-scattered on the Grass "

parts.words: Those of Omar were " Star-scattered on the Grass "
parts.note: quotes FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: the Saki passes among the visitors at the feast, star-scattered on the grass

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat's last quatrain: 'And when like her, oh Saki, you shall pass / Among the Guests Star-scatter'd on the Grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors at a feast are the ones scattered across the lawn in the poem.

clue.text: It does its work when on fire

definitions.text: It does its work when on fire

parts.words: It does its work when on fire
parts.note: not an arsonist or firefighter but a household pot that boils water while sitting on the flames

explanation.surface: Something that works best when ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on fire' suggests burning; it means placed over the fire, as an old kitchen pot was.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for boiling water does its job sitting over a flame or hob.

clue.text: Flier grounded on the line

parts.note: a famous express train, the Flying one, which flies along the rails while staying on the ground

explanation.surface: A pilot is stopped at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Scotsman is the famous London to Edinburgh express; a 'flier' that never leaves the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Scotsman train, a 'flier' that stays on rails, takes its name from a man of Scotland.
